items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We became pretty good friends all through the years.

ctx.x: At time, while you were in college, what music were you listening to? What music was influencing your – what music did you admire at that time?

I grew up listening to Bach – from my mother – and Beethoven. All the classic literature for piano: Debussy, Ravel, and many other things, but those were the main things that she practiced all the time. So I had a knowledge of the good piano literature just by hearing it from her – hearing her teach it during the day, and then after dinner, she usually went into her studio, and when I was in bed, I’d be hearing her practicing. So I had a lot of influence of great piano music. Then I loved Gershwin and Bartok,…
When you were in college, did you have a record player? Radio?

items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: I’ll tell you Ellington wasn’t the greatest reader, did you know that?

ctx.x: Oh that’s just gorgeous. Do you find that in gaining more knowledge about how things work, is it restrictive at all for you? Because you have said that it’s good to be an innocent.

I have not got the capability to study like other guys. It has to be by osmosis or just some other way. And there’s plenty of my friends that work that way that have turned out great music that don’t read well and haven’t studied a lot but write so beautifully. And there might be something to acknowledge that if a person doesn’t have the usual skills, don’t count him out. He might have something else going on that is/are unusual because they aren’t the usual. And in my experience some of my favorite musicians…

reading skills or orchestrating skills, had to pick it up in their own way and have contributed maybe more than anybody else. So there’s something — I’ll tell you Ellington wasn’t the greatest reader, did you know that?

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I said, 'How about Stan Getz?' 'Oh, he’d like that.'

ctx.x: The bottom of – “We are in big trouble, but we think because the King likes you so much, that if you came and played, it might save the situation.” So I said, “I can’t go. I have other concerts that I have to do during this period.” “Can you think of somebody else that the King would like?” I said, “How about Stan Getz?” “Oh, he’d like that.” I guess I’m talking to his social person.
